scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8871: host_2_1_1_1 (10.2.1.2) reports it has lost everything
beyond its own gateway: every 10.200.0.x server times out, and it cannot reach
host_1_1_1_1 in the other pod either. It CAN still ping its gateway 10.2.1.1.
Pod 1 is unaffected -- host_1_1_1_1 reaches the server farm normally. Diagnose.

injection.action: kill the OSPF daemon (ospfd) on router_core_2 and stop watchfrr from respawning it

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router_core_2 ospfd
Mechanism: router_core_2 is pod 2's only way out: switch_dist_2_1's single
  uplink (172.16.0.8/31, area 1) terminates on router_core_2, which as the
  pod-2 ABR carries 10.2.1.0/24 between area 1 and the area-0 backbone. With
  ospfd killed, zebra flushes router_core_2's OSPF routes immediately, so
  pod-2 traffic arriving at router_core_2 has no route and dies there; the
  other routers then age out router_core_2's LSAs and withdraw 10.2.1.0/24.
  Pod 1 (host -> switch_dist_1_1 -> router_core_1 -> router_core_3 -> farm)
  never transits router_core_2, so it stays healthy.
Localization: router_core_2
Root cause: ospfd not running on router_core_2
Fix: restart FRR on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).

Observable note (same kill pattern lab-verified on this topology 2026-07-03):
ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it.
vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO
`router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may
therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is
missing/empty on router_core_2" -- that is the same fault observed at the
config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart FRR / the OSPF daemon on router_core_2 (`service frr restart`).
Unlike the vtysh-provisioned Kath labs, this topology keeps its OSPF config
in /etc/frr/frr.conf (the injection killed the process, not the file), so a
plain restart reloads the full configuration, OSPF re-converges, and pod 2
regains connectivity.
scoring_axes: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2

agent.diagnosis_text:
The ospfd process is not running on router_core_2. The FRR daemons file
(/etc/frr/daemons) correctly marks ospfd=yes, and /etc/frr/frr.conf contains
a well-formed OSPF configuration (router-id 172.16.0.1, three network
statements covering areas 0 and 1). However, a process-table inspection shows
only zebra, mgmtd, and staticd are alive — ospfd is absent. Because no OSPF
daemon is running, the FRR running configuration contains no "router ospf"
stanza, and router_core_2 has only its three directly-connected kernel routes
(172.16.0.0/31, 172.16.0.4/31, 172.16.0.8/31). It neither sends nor receives
OSPF hellos, so it never forms adjacencies with router_core_1 or router_core_3
and learns no routes to 10.1.1.0/24 (pod-1) or 10.200.0.0/24 (server farm).

This is why host_2_1_1_1 can still reach its immediate gateway 10.2.1.1
(switch_dist_2_1, connected directly below router_core_2) but all further
destinations time out: packets that arrive at router_core_2 destined for
10.1.1.x or 10.200.0.x hit a routing black-hole because no OSPF routes exist
in the FIB. Pod 1 is unaffected because router_core_1 and router_core_3 do
run ospfd and have complete OSPF tables.

Root cause: ospfd crashed or was never started on router_core_2, leaving the
router with only connected routes and no OSPF participation.

Corrective fix: Restart the FRR service on router_core_2
(`service frr restart` or `systemctl restart frr`). This will launch ospfd,
which will read the existing frr.conf, form OSPF adjacencies on eth0 (area 0,
toward router_core_1) and eth1 (area 0, toward router_core_3), and install
routes to 10.1.1.0/24 and 10.200.0.0/24, restoring full connectivity for pod 2.

per_axis.rationale: The report repeatedly and explicitly identifies router_core_2 as the affected device where ospfd is not running.
The report explicitly identifies ospfd as not running on router_core_2 (OSPF daemon crashed/never started), matching the required component identification.

per_axis.axis: bonus-scopes-blast-radius: notes pod 1 and the server farm stay healthy, isolating the fault to pod 2's transit through router_core_2
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly says Pod 1 is unaffected (router_core_1 and router_core_3 have OSPF) and discusses the server-farm prefix (10.200.0.0/24), thus isolating the failure to pod 2 via router_core_2.
Recommends restarting the FRR/ospfd daemon on router_core_2 (service frr restart/systemctl restart frr), which matches the expected fix to reload frr.conf and restore OSPF.
